question: What exact title-side policy carries an external NiSourceTexture filename to a loaded texture resource, and is that policy reproducible for standalone or archive-contained NIF documents?

idAssignment.result: RVA-F-0132 is the canonical identifier for this manifest.

dependencies.use: Accepts RVA-F-0124's 383 exact external NiSourceTexture edges, valid non-null filename indices, null Pixel Data references, and privacy boundary without reopening retail NIF payloads.
Accepts RVA-F-0131's exact NiSourceTexture reader, external filename carrier, runtime field positions, and read-only retention boundary.
Accepts RVA-F-0072's identification of 0x8280F578 as the NtCreateFile wrapper and the maintained ReXGlue result that a rootless guest name is not made relative to game: or d:.

scope.boundary: The packet follows the exact external filename from the accepted NiSourceTexture reader through its title-owned runtime name, lazy resource request, file-object creation, and NtCreateFile boundary. It inspects only direct helpers required to characterize that path. It does not inventory filenames, decode texture payloads, inspect the renderer, or perform an executable-wide file-open search. A bounded runtime observation identifies one concrete stream-provider vtable; its callbacks, exact vtable constructors, and immediate storage helpers establish static initialization and registration mechanics. Static corroboration resolves the observed shared-provider attachment caller and the complete raw direct-call set for the separate candidate-collection wrapper. Runtime registration order for that provider, global-list population, and filesystem roots remain outside the accepted result.

acceptedPopulation.contract: Every accepted source has Use External equal to one, a valid non-null File Name string index, and the standard null Pixel Data reference.
acceptedPopulation.reuseOnly: No retail string was decoded for this packet. The population is reused only as an aggregate accepted source class.

serializedCarrier.result: The external File Name fixed string is read into object +0x30 and materialized by 0x823941D8 into the runtime filename at object +0x34.

streamResolution.result: The reader can consult a candidate collection and the provider at stream +0x1C0 before retaining the runtime filename. A new-game map observation identifies provider vtable 0x82161E9C with lookup 0x82C82BC8 and registration 0x82C82C08. Static constructors and table insertion mechanics are identified below; a fresh observation binds the sampled provider and stream to the shared globals, but not to a particular construction call, registration sequence, search root, or owning-NIF/archive relationship. The static path 0x82C831A8 -> 0x8235ED80 attaches the provider returned by 0x82C8D918 to the stream referenced by 0x8314F268; the getter retains a constructed provider at 0x8314F244.

lazyResourceRequest.result: When no resource is retained, 0x82391A20 passes the runtime filename through the singleton returned by 0x82393B10 and its vtable +0x0C method 0x82393D40. A successful result is retained at object +0x3C.

fileAndDecodeBoundary.result: 0x82393D40 creates a file object from the supplied runtime filename, requires the file object's success check, and only then invokes its owned converter through vtable +0x08. The converter's non-null return is the first proved loaded-resource carrier.

lookupChain.release: 0x823914A0 releases only the retained object +0x3C resource through its existing ownership path. No filename search policy is inferred from release behavior.

byteInterpretation.proved: The runtime path is a NUL-terminated byte string. 0x8280F578 passes it to RtlInitAnsiString before NtCreateFile.
byteInterpretation.terminator: The first zero byte terminates the runtime filename; bytes after an embedded NUL do not participate in the file request.
byteInterpretation.encoding: RtlInitAnsiString establishes an ANSI_STRING byte carrier, not a proved text encoding. ASCII, UTF-8, an Xbox code page, and Unicode interpretation are not promoted.

filenamePolicy.directName: With the optional prefix global null, 0x823941D8 copies the fixed-string bytes to object +0x34 without normalization. The image's initial word at 0x82F8E594 is zero.
filenamePolicy.separatorHandling: The optional rebuild helper recognizes both backslash and forward slash as existing separators when joining components. Prefix normalizer 0x82468D48 converts forward slashes to backslashes and collapses repeated backslashes after the leading bytes while preserving leading duplicates; it operates on the prefix only. No proved step normalizes separators in the direct unprefixed source name.
filenamePolicy.absoluteAndRelative: The optional split/rebuild path preserves an existing drive and directory component and inserts its prefix before the filename stem. The direct path neither requires nor rejects absolute or relative spelling. No policy selects one class as valid.
filenamePolicy.dotComponents: No admitted title helper resolves, rejects, or otherwise assigns policy to dot or dot-dot components before NtCreateFile. Host behavior must not be substituted for an unproved title rule.
filenamePolicy.case: The source spelling is preserved through the proved title chain. 0x8280F578 supplies object-attribute flag 0x40 to NtCreateFile, providing a case-insensitive object-name request at that boundary; final mounted-source or host duplicate behavior is not thereby proved. The provider table helper 0x822EF528 compares NUL-terminated keys byte for byte; that local comparison performs no case folding.
filenamePolicy.prefixDirectoryExtensionRoot: The direct file-open chain adds no prefix, directory, extension, game:, d:, or device root. An optional global directory prefix can be inserted by 0x823941D8, but the image initializes its carrier to null and no direct caller of setter 0x82393E48 was found in the bounded reference query. Indirect setup and runtime value remain unresolved.
filenamePolicy.bufferBoundary: The optional split/rebuild uses a 260-byte destination. This establishes a bounded internal carrier, but the bounded path does not prove a complete malformed-name classification for every failed rebuild.

provedOrder: NiSourceTexture reader may replace the serialized name through its stream-owned provider/candidate mechanism.
Lazy resource creation later opens the one runtime filename retained at object +0x34.
A valid file object is passed to the resource converter.
unresolved: Concrete candidate roots and their deterministic order
Original provider class name, whether the resolved getter invocation took its constructor branch, and the registration sequence used by the observed runtime instance
Whether any candidate is relative to the owning NIF
Whether any candidate is relative to the containing archive
The runtime population and namespace ownership of the provider table and optional global object list, including any archive or mounted-device relationship
Duplicate-source precedence across registrations, provider candidates, and the optional global list; local equal-key table assignment alone does not establish source order
Runtime value and owner of the optional global prefix
searchPolicy.directOpenQualification: The proved final open is filesystem-style NtCreateFile through the title file abstraction. A preceding injected provider can choose or substitute the name, so this does not prove that the complete title lookup policy is filesystem-only.

failureBehavior.missingOrOpenFailure: If file-object creation fails or its success check is false, 0x82393D40 returns no resource. 0x82391A20 leaves object +0x3C null and returns normally; the already loaded NIF object is not rejected by this lazy failure path.
failureBehavior.unsupportedOrDecodeFailure: If the file opens but converter vtable +0x08 returns null, the same null-resource outcome is retained. The bounded path proves no fallback texture installation.
failureBehavior.retry: The lazy 0x82391A20 -> 0x82393D40 boundary tries the retained runtime filename once and contains no second-root retry. Earlier candidate/provider behavior in the stream reader exists, but its concrete candidates and failure ordering are unresolved.
failureBehavior.malformedName: NUL termination and the optional 260-byte rebuild boundary are proved. Rejection behavior for absolute names, dot components, invalid byte sequences, and rebuild overflow is not completely classified.
failureBehavior.ownership: Temporary file objects are released on both success and failure paths. A successful converted resource is retained at object +0x3C until the existing release path clears it.

implementationReadiness.standaloneReason: A standalone NIF provides the serialized filename but not the title stream candidate collection, provider-container population, optional global object-list state, concrete roots, deterministic source order, duplicate policy, or optional prefix value. The observed provider vtable does not supply that missing state.
implementationReadiness.archiveReason: The accepted chain does not bind stream provider +0x1C0 or candidate collection +0x124 to the containing FPK, the NIF entry location, or any archive-relative namespace. Archive membership therefore supplies no proved lookup owner or precedence rule.
implementationReadiness.authorized: No Studio external texture lookup is authorized by this manifest. Existing lossless source metadata retention remains valid.
implementationReadiness.targetAuditReason: The accepted evidence supplies no independently reproducible bounded root or matching rule. The privacy-preserving target audit must not run.

currentEvidence.method: Foreground read-only method-table, function, instruction, memory-word, string, reference, and exact raw direct-call queries were combined with narrow generated-code corroboration for admitted methods. Default-off runtime probes captured numeric provider identity and, in a fresh normal new-game map load, shared-global matches and bounded pre-hook observations. No retail filename text or texture payload was analyzed for lookup policy.

entries.result: The exact source reader materializes the external fixed string into object +0x34 and exposes the stream-owned candidate/provider boundary.
The retained runtime filename is opened once; a valid file object is converted, and only a non-null converted resource is retained.
The runtime filename reaches NtCreateFile as a NUL-terminated ANSI_STRING with root directory 0xFFFFFFFD and object-attribute flag 0x40; the chain adds no title prefix or extension.
The image initializes the prefix carrier to null. A setter and bounded split/rebuild mechanics exist, but no direct setter caller or runtime owner was found in the admitted reference query.
The packet reuses only the accepted aggregate of 383 external filename references and does not decode their text.

Eight capped samples during a new-game map load identified one provider vtable and its two slot targets. Static references and exact generated callbacks corroborate the captured dispatch identity, but not lookup success or provider population.

entries.role: static provider construction and table population mechanics
entries.result: Two exact vtable construction sites establish empty-table initialization with global-list fallback enabled. Byte-exact lookup and equal-key object replacement are identified; these static methods alone do not establish runtime source order or population.

The shared getter constructs the captured vtable type, and 0x82C831A8 passes that provider to a locked setter for stream +0x1C0. The global storage path differs from the previously identified enclosing-object field; the static path alone does not identify a runtime instance or its executed caller.

Sixteen lookup samples from 0x82391CE4 matched the provider and stream to both shared globals. Checked provider +0x14 entry counts were 0, 1, or 2. The earlier capped registration observations belonged to a different provider and cannot establish the matched provider's registration order.

entries.role: resolved shared-provider attachment caller and candidate-collection boundary
entries.result: The observed LR is the return from sub_82C833A0's direct setter call. That function obtains r4 from the shared getter immediately before loading shared stream global 0x8314F268 into r3. It contains no direct stream +0x124 access, provider-registration call, or global-list-root reference. A separate path reads stream +0x124 and conditionally passes an opaque caller value to 0x82466BD8, which mutates candidate collection +0x10C. The canonical listing has no decoded references to its wrapper 0x82C832A0, but an exact raw direct-call scan finds three untruncated callers and narrows the forwarded value to caller-object fields +0x10 or +0x4 without assigning either field a root or namespace.

currentEvidence.privacy: Static findings and probe output retain numeric code, slot, field, and runtime identity information only. No retail filename text, texture values, payload bytes, per-file hashes, or filename-to-target mapping was analyzed or promoted. No asset checkout was queried or modified by this investigation; the isolated title consumed a disposable runtime copy through its normal load path.

boundedNegatives: The ANSI_STRING carrier does not prove ASCII, UTF-8, a code page, or Unicode semantics.
No exact title rule is promoted for dot components, absolute-name acceptance, malformed byte sequences, or all overlength outcomes.

Shared-global pointer equality plus LR 0x82C8345C identifies the executed pre-hook attachment call in sub_82C833A0 and its immediately preceding getter invocation. It does not prove that the getter took its constructor branch, that the setter completed, or that an earlier session used the same instance. Candidate roots, registration sequence for the shared provider, owning-NIF or archive relationship, and mounted-device ownership remain unresolved. Local equal-key replacement does not establish duplicate-source precedence.

The resolved attachment path contains no direct candidate-collection, provider-registration, or global-list access. The separate +0x124 path mutates candidate collection +0x10C from an opaque caller argument. Its complete raw direct-call set narrows that argument to fields +0x10 or +0x4 of three caller objects, but does not establish a root, source order, namespace owner, archive relationship, or target-container rule.
The null initial prefix carrier and absence of a direct setter reference do not prove that an indirect runtime setup can never install a prefix.
Object-attribute flag 0x40 describes the direct object-name request; it does not prove duplicate precedence or every mounted source's host comparison behavior.
A null loaded resource proves neither visible rendering behavior nor a user-facing fallback; renderer consumption remains outside scope.
No target container or encoding is promoted because no independently reproducible root and matching rule are proved.
No Studio implementation, UI, texture decoder, preview, GPU upload, sampling, rendering, embedded pixel-data support, or writer is authorized.

catalogPromotion.result: The observed provider vtable, its lookup and registration targets, and the runtime-corroborated attachment caller are promoted with narrow roles. Static construction, registration, and candidate-collection mechanics are maintained in this topic; complete layout, runtime population, and namespace ownership are not cataloged.

guards: Do not inspect the asset inventory until separate evidence proves an independently reproducible bounded root and matching rule.
Do not infer owning-directory, containing-archive, installation-root, case, separator, or duplicate policy from retail filename spelling or Gamebryo convention.
Do not treat the direct NtCreateFile request as proof that the unresolved stream provider is filesystem-only.
Do not expose, retain, hash, extract, or map retail filename or texture payload data.
Do not implement Studio lookup, texture decoding, GPU work, rendering, editing, conversion, export, or writing from this packet.
conclusion: The exact title chain materializes NiSourceTexture external fixed strings into object +0x34 and later passes the retained byte name through a lazy file-object and converter path to NtCreateFile. A normal new-game map load identifies provider vtable 0x82161E9C and its lookup and registration callbacks. Static construction starts an empty 37-bucket table and enables optional global-list fallback; table keys compare byte for byte, and equal-key registration replaces the stored object. The runtime-observed LR 0x82C8345C resolves to sub_82C833A0, which invokes the shared getter and immediately attaches its result to stream global 0x8314F268. A separate static path through 0x82C831A8 reads stream +0x124 and conditionally mutates candidate collection +0x10C from an opaque caller argument. Three exact raw callers narrow that argument to caller-object fields +0x10 or +0x4, but do not identify their semantic owner. Neither bounded path identifies shared-provider registration, global-list population, a reproducible root, archive relationship, source precedence, or target-container policy. Neither standalone-NIF nor archive-contained-NIF lookup is reproducible from these local mechanics, so the Studio lookup and target-container gates remain closed.

observation.configuration: Windows x64 Release, default-off init-only probe enabled for an isolated normal title launch.
observation.buildProvenance: The Windows Release executable reports base 460d3e8fa39c269b5152d75edcdd754b71cd2123 with local modifications; its probe sources match instrumentRevision.
observation.scene: The owner confirmed the main menu without a probe sample, then confirmed a loaded new-game map. The map load produced eight samples of the same stream/provider/vtable identity; the process later exited normally.
observation.captureBoundary: The probe reads only stream +0x1C0, the provider vtable word, and the +0x8/+0xC callback words. It captures no name, payload, callback return, or loaded-resource result. The cap was reached during the first observed burst, so other providers and scenes remain unclassified.

staticCorroboration.vtableReferences: Read-only reference queries identify 0x82161EA4 -> 0x82C82BC8 and 0x82161EA8 -> 0x82C82C08, matching the runtime slot words.
staticCorroboration.lookup: The exact generated 0x82C82BC8 body delegates its provider, name, and current-object arguments to 0x822EF3A8 and returns that result. The helper first queries the provider +0x8 container. On a miss, a nonzero provider byte +0x1C permits traversal of the object list rooted at 0x82F8E660 via next +0x2C, excluding the current object and checking a candidate +0x30 name carrier.
staticCorroboration.registration: The exact 0x82C82C08 body retains the supplied object and passes provider +0x8, the name argument, and the object carrier to 0x822EF668. This helper hashes and compares NUL-terminated byte keys, inserts a missing key at the bucket head, or assigns the object through the existing entry +0x8 for an equal key.
staticCorroboration.analysisLimits: Ghidra truncates several functions at save thunks or unsupported instructions. Exact raw split-constant candidates locate two vtable constructions outside decoded function bodies; bounded memory words and narrow generated functions confirm the stated writes. The fully decoded 0x822EF528 corroborates byte-key lookup. Candidate matches alone do not prove executable code or uninterrupted register lifetime.

runtimeProvider.qualification: The observed vtable is a concrete provider identity, not an original class name, a filesystem root, or a successful lookup result. The fresh run matches its sampled provider and stream to the shared globals, and static corroboration resolves the observed attachment caller's getter-to-setter path. Whether that getter invocation constructed the instance, the completed setter result, registration sequence, optional global-list population, and namespace ownership remain unresolved.

constructionAndRegistration.method: Static image words, decoded lookup helper, and exact-function generated corroboration; no additional runtime observation.

initializers.result: 0x82C82C80 calls 0x822EF900 with argument 1, writes provider +0x20 = 3, and installs vtable 0x82161E9C. The base initializer calls 0x822EF168(provider +0x8, 37), installs container vtable 0x82161ED0, sets provider byte +0x18 = 1, and stores its argument at provider byte +0x1C. Thus this construction enables the lookup helper's optional global-list fallback.
initializers.inlineResult: The exact path at 0x82C84D38 requests 0x24 bytes, performs the same base initialization and vtable/+0x20 writes on the allocated object, and stores it at enclosing object +0x14 at 0x82C84D74 before retaining it through provider +0x4. The enclosing object's original type and its connection to stream +0x1C0 are not assigned.

constructionAndRegistration.initialTable: 0x822EF168 stores the supplied bucket count at container +0x4, clears entry count +0xC, allocates four bytes per bucket, stores the bucket-array pointer at +0x8, and zero-fills that array. The admitted provider construction therefore begins with 37 empty buckets; it does not preload archive names.
constructionAndRegistration.lookup: 0x822EF528 computes a 32-bit multiply-by-33/add hash over signed byte values until NUL, selects a bucket modulo container +0x4, follows entry +0x0 links, and compares entry +0x4 keys byte for byte. A matching entry supplies its object at +0x8 through refcounted assignment 0x821B2440 (RVA-SYM-0136); no match returns zero.
constructionAndRegistration.registration: 0x822EF668 uses the same hash and exact-byte comparison. A missing key allocates an entry through container vtable +0xC, assigns its key/object through vtable +0x4 (0x822EF288 for the initialized table), inserts it at the bucket head, and increments container +0xC. An equal key branches at 0x822EF710 to 0x822EF7F8 and calls 0x821B2440 on existing entry +0x8; it does not add a second entry or increment the count on that branch.
constructionAndRegistration.keyStorage: 0x822EF288 tests container byte +0x10, which is provider byte +0x18. The admitted initializer sets it to 1, selecting allocation of a NUL-inclusive key buffer and the copy helper before object assignment. The other branch stores the supplied key pointer. No concrete retail key is inspected.
constructionAndRegistration.qualification: These are static mechanics for the admitted constructors and table methods. Runtime observations below identify shared-global pointer matches and bounded entry counts, but not constructor calls, keys, lookup results, fallback execution, or the shared provider's completed registration sequence. Other mutation paths, global-list population, and roots remain unresolved. Equal-key replacement is a local table rule, not archive or filesystem precedence.

streamAttachment.providerConstruction: The getter returns the non-null global value. On the null path it requests 0x24 bytes, calls 0x82C82C80 on the allocated object, stores the result at 0x8314F244, and retains it through object +0x4. This is a separate storage path from the enclosing object +0x14 populated by 0x82C84B58.
streamAttachment.attachment: 0x82C831A8 calls the getter, loads the stream pointer from 0x8314F268, and calls 0x8235ED80(stream, provider) at 0x82C831D0. It then calls 0x82361260 with the same stream and its second incoming argument before dispatching stream virtual methods. This establishes attachment before those later calls on the admitted path, not the full load or registration order.
streamAttachment.assignment: The setter preserves its incoming stream and provider, enters the critical section at 0x82F8E350, calls 0x82347100(stream +0x1C0, provider), and leaves that critical section. The assignment helper compares the old and new pointers, leaves an identical pointer unchanged, otherwise releases the previous non-null object, stores the new pointer, and retains a non-null replacement through object +0x4.
streamAttachment.qualification: These are static call and field facts for one attachment path. The fresh observation below matches the sampled provider and stream to these globals. Its LR resolves to a separate getter-to-setter call in sub_82C833A0, recorded below. The global addresses do not identify a filesystem root, archive namespace, complete lifetime, or deterministic population order.

observedAttachmentCaller.result: sub_82C833A0 moves the getter result into setter r4, loads setter r3 from shared stream global 0x8314F268, and calls the setter. Twelve existing pre-hook samples from return address 0x82C8345C carried the same stream/provider pair as the admitted lookup samples and shared globals.
observedAttachmentCaller.candidateCollectionBoundary: The exact sub_82C833A0 body contains no stream +0x124 access, provider-registration call, or global-list-root reference. The separate sub_82C831A8 path reads stream +0x124 at 0x82C8320C and calls 0x82466BD8 at 0x82C83224 only when both the collection and its third argument are non-null. 0x82466BD8 clears candidate collection byte +0x10C for null or empty input and otherwise mutates the +0x10C subobject through bounded string helpers. sub_82C832A0 forwards its r5 input unchanged to this path. The canonical listing has no decoded references to that wrapper; an exact raw scan of initialized executable words finds three direct calls at 0x82C63064, 0x82C83678, and 0x82E74960, with no truncation. Narrow exact-function corroboration shows that sub_82C62FC0 supplies caller object +0x10, while sub_82C83640 and sub_82E74920 each supply caller object +0x4. Their return addresses 0x82C63068, 0x82C8367C, and 0x82E74964 are the complete admitted runtime caller discriminator set.
observedAttachmentCaller.boundedNegative: Across sub_82C833A0, sub_82C831A8, sub_82C832A0, sub_82466BD8, and the three raw direct callers, no shared-provider registration call or global-list-root reference is established. The +0x10 and +0x4 candidate-input fields are not bound to an owning NIF, archive, mounted source, independently reproducible root, or target-container rule. Tracing all three caller families would widen beyond the runtime-selectable discriminator.
observedAttachmentCaller.qualification: The pre-hook observation does not prove setter completion or that the getter took its constructor branch. The candidate mutation does not establish lookup order, duplicate-source precedence, or a target-container matching rule.

lookup.result: Every sample had readable global words equal to the sampled provider and stream, vtable 0x82161E9C, lookup slot 0x82C82BC8, and registration slot 0x82C82C08.
lookup.entryCountQualification: All count reads succeeded. These snapshots show local table state at lookup entry; they do not identify keys, explain each transition, or prove a successful lookup.

attachment.result: Twelve setter pre-hook samples from LR 0x82C8345C carried the same stream/provider pair as the lookup samples. One from LR 0x82C98B4C carried a different pair. Three from LR 0x82C73598 carried the matched provider with another stream.
attachment.qualification: Incoming arguments are observations before the setter body, not completed reference assignments. Static corroboration now identifies LR 0x82C8345C as the direct setter call in sub_82C833A0; the original method name remains unresolved.

registration.result: All samples used one different provider pointer with the same expected vtable and readable entry counts. The 64-attempt cap was reached before the first admitted lookup sample.
registration.qualification: The cap prevents a conclusion about later registration calls for the matched shared provider. These pre-hook observations do not prove successful insertion, equal-key replacement, or completed registration order.

sharedInstanceObservation.captureBoundary: The process emitted 99 numeric events: 16 lookup, 16 attachment, 64 registration, and one cap marker for each hook. Event numbers order emitted pre-hook observations only, not completed calls or cross-thread transactions. Reads were bounded to stream/provider identity, callback words, two shared globals, and the expected-vtable-gated entry count. No name, key hash, payload, object contents, callback return, or guest write was captured. A fresh-session pointer match does not retroactively identify an earlier session instance.
